context_title:
Create a complete, production-ready, highly optimized rendering system that replicates a dynamic, liquid-like translucent software material for UI components. The system must be built natively using Swift, Metal, Core Animation, and SwiftUI. It must handle real-time spatial physics, adaptive lighting, and complex geometry morphing. The implementation must include all necessary files, unabridged code, and correct APIs, following this exact step-by-step technical architecture:
Step 1: Establish the Core Animation Layer (The Custom CALayer Subclass)
Implement a custom  CALayer  subclass that serves as the underlying rendering engine.
•	The layer must intercept the display pipeline to perform physically-based rendering (PBR) operations.
•	Integrate a custom Metal-backed compositor within this layer. It must execute custom fragment shaders that calculate real-time raymarching, adaptive frosting, translucency, and depth-based shadows.
•	The layer must continuously read the screen-space coordinates and device motion data to dynamically adjust the refractive index and specular highlights (simulating light bending through a fluid medium).
•	Ensure the layer supports an adaptive tone-mapping pass. It must dynamically sample the luminance of the content directly behind it to adjust the brightness and edge diffusion (rim lighting) of the shape, preventing visual bleed or illegibility on dark or light backgrounds.
Step 2: Implement the Interactive Physics and Touch Engine
Develop a robust physics engine tied directly to user interaction ( UITouch  or SwiftUI gesture equivalents) that alters the geometry of the material layer.
•	Integrate a mass-spring-damper physical simulation model that triggers upon interaction.
•	The shape must not simply scale down when pressed. Instead, it must compute a Signed Distance Field (SDF) of the provided geometry bounding box.
•	Upon touch, the system must push the SDF boundaries inward towards the touch epicenter, modifying the normal vectors in real-time. This normal vector shift must instantly update the Metal shader to shift the specular highlights, simulating a physical “dent” in the fluid surface.
•	Implement an explicit shape-resolving mechanism. To prevent the bounding box highlight from bleeding outside complex geometries, the system must enforce a hard clipping mask (e.g., matching the exact Bezier path or concentric corner radiuses) during the final compositing pass.
Step 3: Develop the Geometric Container for Shape Morphing
Build a container wrapper that manages multiple instances of the custom layer to prevent GPU overdraw and enable geometry blending.
•	Create a container view system that intercepts all child components using this material.
•	Instead of rendering multiple independent overlapping layers (which causes redundant double-translucency rendering passes), the container must extract the SDF data from all child components.
•	Mathematically merge these individual SDFs into a single continuous unified geometry mesh using a Metaballs or raymarched blending algorithm based on a defined spacing threshold.
•	Submit this single unified mesh to the Metal rendering pipeline, ensuring that adjacent or colliding elements fluidly morph into one another without rendering duplicate refraction passes.
Step 4: Construct the UI Framework Wrappers
Expose the complex rendering pipeline through clean, native API wrappers for both imperative and declarative UI frameworks.
•	For the imperative framework: Create a view modifier system that hooks into the layout engine to establish concentric corner configurations dynamically. It must calculate corner radiuses that run parallel to the parent window or hardware screen boundaries without requiring explicit hardcoded values.
•	For the declarative framework: Develop a custom view modifier and a container protocol. The modifier must accept material descriptors (e.g., thickness, tint) and a defined  Shape . The modifier must seamlessly map the declarative  Shape  into the underlying SDF for the Metal shader and attach the spring physics interaction model automatically.
•	The declarative container must coordinate the shape morphing across all identified child modifiers.
Provide the entire implementation in complete, compilable Swift and Metal code, including the layer definitions, the Metal shader functions, the SDF math functions, the physical interaction extensions, and the final declarative view modifiers. Do not use placeholders or simplifications.
